sources.citation: van den Berg, René. 2021. Un-Austronesian features of Malol, an Oceanic language of PNG. Slides presented at APLL13, Edinburgh, June 2021 (28 slides, 6-up on 5 PDF pages; author-posted on ResearchGate 26 Jul 2023, publication 372627981). Glottolog ref 586105 (the only descriptive item Glottolog lists).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Phonology is inventory-level only: slide 6 '5 vowels, 14 consonants'; slides 7-14 four falling diphthongs <ie ea uo oa>, no voiced stops, word-final palatals /tʃ ɲ/ from *-Vni metathesis. Words 'stress', 'accent', 'prosody', 'syllable' do not occur. Data source given as 'van den Berg-Klingeman (in preparation)'. Obtained via the the Internet Archive copy of the author's public ResearchGate PDF (live host blocks our network).

sources.citation: Whitacre, Steve. 1984. Arop Phonemic Statement. MS, SIL Ukarumpa, 37 pp. (SIL archives 58388). Arop dialect of Sissano (arop1242), a sister village of Malol.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: AROP, not Malol (p. 1 names Malol as one of the three Sissano villages but gives no Malol data). Sec. 6.1 'Phonemic status of stress' (printed pp. 17-19): 'Stress is predictable in most instances in Arop'; trisyllables stress the 2nd syllable except verbs; verbs primary stress on 1st syllable of the root, secondary on the pronoun; disyllabic modifiers 2nd syllable; disyllabic nouns 1st; reduplicated nouns 1st, reduplicated modifiers 2nd; a few minimal pairs, low functional load. Cannot stand for Malol.

sources.citation: Friederici, Georg. 1913. Untersuchungen über eine melanesische Wanderstrasse. Mitteilungen aus den deutschen Schutzgebieten, Ergänzungsheft 7 (scanned PDF, archive.org MittSchutzErganz_7, 26 MB; only the scanned text was saved).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Carries accent diacritics on scattered Malol forms and a remark on Sissano final-syllable prominence; the page images would let the diacritics be read reliably (scanned is poor), but it is a wordlist, not a rule.

sources.citation: Friederici, Georg. 1913. Wissenschaftliche Ergebnisse einer amtlichen Forschungsreise nach dem Bismarck-Archipel im Jahre 1908, III: Untersuchungen über eine melanesische Wanderstrasse. Mitteilungen aus den deutschen Schutzgebieten, Ergänzungsheft 7. Berlin: Mittler. (Glottolog ref 71662, 'wordlist' for Malol.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Malol rule. Malol forms appear scattered in comparative word discussions with accent diacritics (e.g. 'Malol: räi (rat)', 'neü', 'änö'), scanned unreliable. The only prosodic remark (Lautlehre introduction, p. 19-20) concerns Sissano, not Malol: 'in Neu-Guinea ist mir in Sissano die singende Wiedergabe der betonten Endsilbe in vielen Worten aufgefallen' (impressionistic: many Sissano words have a stressed, sung final syllable).

sources.citation: Friederici, Georg. 1912. Wissenschaftliche Ergebnisse.., II: Beiträge zur Völker- und Sprachenkunde von Deutsch-Neuguinea. Mitteilungen aus den deutschen Schutzgebieten, Ergänzungsheft 5.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Malol appears only ethnographically and in one phonetic aside ('in Malol und Aröp wird das t z. T. sehr weich ausgesprochen'). Accent remarks are about Barriai and 'all Melanesian languages known to me' ('dem Akzent kommt im Barriai, wie in allen mir bekannt gewordenen melanesischen Sprachen, nicht die Bedeutung und das Feststehende zu wie bei uns'); nothing Malol-specific.

sources.note: Not opened: no file attached in the 2015, 2020 or live catalogue captures ('Requires: Fieldworks Language Explorer'). Sibling 2013-15 SIL-PNG Tentative Grammar Descriptions opened in this reading (Gabadi, Angaataha, Miniafia, Buhutu, Kalo, Tairuma) have a sec. 2 'Writing system and sounds' that lists letters only and is silent on stress, so this one is unlikely to carry a stress rule.
